Rockford's aerospace supply chain: does your NDT certification sit under SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410?

Rockford makes aircraft systems. The operation now part of Collins Aerospace has long designed and built aircraft electric power systems, ram air turbines and the actuators that move flaps and slats. Woodward finished a large transformation of its Loves Park campus in 2024 for manufacturing, testing and aftermarket service of aircraft fuel controls, with about 1,100 people on site. AAR maintains aircraft at Chicago Rockford International Airport, and gear makers, heat treaters, platers and machine shops across Winnebago, Boone and Ogle counties supply them all. Ask three Rockford employers which certification scheme they use and you can get three different answers.

Answer one: the machine shop, heat treater or finisher shipping flight hardware

Suppliers to airframe, engine and systems makers usually find NAS 410, or EN 4179 on European work, in the quality clauses of their purchase orders. The requirement flows down to whichever company tests the parts, so a heat treater running a fluorescent penetrant line after quench, or a gear shop running magnetic particle on carburized steel, can be certifying people to NAS 410 because of a clause written further up the chain. Under NAS 410 the shop designates a Responsible Level 3 (RL3) in writing; the RL3 approves the written practice, the training, the examiners and any outside agency, and answers to customer and Nadcap AC7114 auditors.

For a technician joining such a shop, two things stand out. The RL3 decides what your earlier SNT-TC-1A training, experience and certification are worth, and that certificate alone does not meet a NAS 410 requirement. And in penetrant and magnetic particle, the methods Rockford suppliers lean on, the formal training minimums in NAS 410 run ahead of the SNT-TC-1A recommendations. The aerospace penetrant testing guide and magnetic particle testing training describe the work.

Answer two: the repair and overhaul side

Aftermarket work on fuel controls and aircraft maintenance at the airport answer to engine makers, airlines and the FAA. The FAA itself certifies no NDT personnel. Advisory Circular 65-31B treats a handful of standards as acceptable, from NAS 410 and ATA Specification 105 to SNT-TC-1A, and each Part 145 repair station works to the one its repair station manual and its customers' contracts name. A hangar job can therefore sit under a different document from the machine shop down the road. Ask the Level 3 which standard and revision the manual names before you assume. Aviation NDT consulting covers repair-station NDT programs.

Answer three: the plant, structural and nuclear side

Not every Rockford NDT job touches aircraft. Gear makers and fabricators selling to industrial customers, structural steel to AWS D1.1, boilers and pressure vessels to ASME, and outage work at Byron Generating Station, where in-service inspection follows ASME Section XI and the ASNT documents it references, all run on the employer's own SNT-TC-1A-based written practice or, where a code demands it, on CP-189. A Rockford technician may hold certifications from both worlds over a career, moving between them as orders shift.

What to keep, whichever door you walk through

Both schemes are employer-based: you are certified by the company, and the certification ends with the job. What survives is the record behind it. Keep course outlines showing hours and instructors, an experience log signed by a Level 3 and broken down by method and part type, every general, specific and practical examination result, your vision records, and each certification letter with the standard and revision printed on it. A Rockford RL3 can only credit what is on paper.

Supplier quality managers running both schemes should keep them in separate written practices, time the move of the NAS 410 written practice to Revision 6, out since December 2025, with their customers, and expect a Nadcap or customer auditor to follow a signed report back through each inspector's file. Atlantis can carry the document load through NAS 410 audit documentation support, assembling and checking that file set while your RL3 keeps approval, alongside SNT-TC-1A and Nadcap audit support.

Where Atlantis fits for Rockford

In Rockford, Atlantis works on the SNT-TC-1A side and on the audit file. Trainees take theory online, self-paced, with our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT) answering questions; practise penetrant, magnetic particle and UT setups in the Practical NDT simulator; and complete hands-on training and the practical examination at the employer's plant to its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Rockford. Supplier quality teams use our Level III consulting for SNT-TC-1A written practices that carry customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114 requirements, for procedures, for Level I and II examinations and for outside agency Level III coverage. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to Rock River Valley suppliers. Whether outside coursework earns credit toward a NAS 410 certification at a Rockford shop is a question for that shop's RL3, best asked before you enroll. The NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A comparison and NAS 410 explained go further.
